Personalized PageRank Results for Signaling Network

receptor.ppr.Rd

A list containing the results of running the personalized PageRank (PPR) algorithm on sig.graph. The PPR algorithm evaluates the regulatory potential of receptors on target genes within an intra-cellular signaling network. This list provides a prior model and the necessary parameters for refining the PPR matrix.

Usage

receptor.ppr

Format

A list with three elements:

ppr

A numeric matrix representing the personalized PageRank results. Rows correspond to receptors (source nodes), and columns correspond to targets. Each entry reflects the regulatory potential of a receptor on a target gene.

ltf

A numeric value representing the quantile threshold learned via NicheNet integration. Entries in the ppr matrix with regulatory potential below this quantile are set to zero, effectively pruning low-confidence interactions.

tfs

A character vector of transcription factor (TF) gene names available in the ppr matrix. These TFs are potential targets of receptors in the regulatory network.

Source

Applying igraph's page_rank function on sig.graph.

Details

The ppr matrix provides a prior model of receptor-target regulatory potential, where the regulatory effect of each receptor is evaluated using personalized PageRank with receptors as source nodes. The ltf threshold is used to prune low-confidence interactions, ensuring only high-confidence regulatory potentials are retained.

This object is a key output of the NicheNet integration pipeline implemented by Ominipath, supporting downstream analyses such as upstream signaling pathway (USP) inference and regulatory network refinement.

See also

sig.graph, gr.graph

Examples

# Access the PPR matrix
head(receptor.ppr$ppr)
